subject: Two hexos suites self-declare @catalog status GATE but nothing calls them
description:
md100-cmdlet-help.test.js:8 and terminal-async-output.test.js:8 both carry '@catalog status GATE'. Verified by explicit grep against deploy.sh, _tools/deploy/post-verify.sh and package.json: ZERO references to either filename anywhere. They run only if a human runs them by hand. md100-cmdlet-help asserts 58 checks and terminal-async-output 10 (it reports as 'N clean / 0 still broken' rather than 'N/M passed'), and both pass today -- this is not a red suite, it is a suite nobody reads. Found by the adversarial reviewer while mapping the 11 Chromium suites for task 352; I had surveyed the same files and missed it. This is exactly the defect the CATALOG rule exists to surface, in its most awkward form: CATALOG.md's wiring column is DERIVED from the tree and cannot lie, but '@catalog status' is HAND-WRITTEN, so a file can still claim to be a gate while nothing invokes it. Decide per suite: wire it into deploy.sh gate 3.8's loop (that loop is the list, so adding a member is one line), or demote the header to TOOL so the claim matches reality. Do NOT leave the header saying GATE while the tree says otherwise. Consider also whether gen-catalog.py should FLAG the contradiction -- a status of GATE with an empty wiring column is a checkable inconsistency, and catching it automatically is worth more than catching these two by hand.
[2026-09-06 20:44] SECOND DEFECT IN md100-cmdlet-help, found while adopting 352, and it INTERACTS with the wire-or-demote decision. Its top-level catch reads: runExamplesInBrowser(HELP).then(...).catch((e)=>{ console.error('harness error, nothing verified:', e.message); process.exit(2); }). The MESSAGE is right -- a harness error is not a verdict on the product -- but the EXIT CODE is exactly wrong under this repo's convention: seven call sites in post-verify.sh read rc 2 as 'puppeteer unavailable, SKIPPED' and set NO divergence flag. So the moment this suite is wired into a gate, a genuine harness error becomes a silent skip rather than a blocked deploy: the failure mode taskboard 345 exists to prevent, arriving through the exit code instead of the message. It is harmless TODAY only because nothing calls this suite -- which is the very thing 353 is about. DECIDE TOGETHER, do not wire it without fixing this: if wired, that catch must exit 1 (node's own default for an unhandled rejection, and what _tools/hexos/harness-forensics.js emits) and print a line containing FAIL plus the words 'harness fault', which is the marker deploy.sh gate 3.7 and post-verify check 4f now branch on to say 'not a verdict on the shell' instead of 'regressed'. NOTE ALSO for 352 adoption: because that .catch HANDLES every rejection thrown inside runExamplesInBrowser, the harness-forensics process handlers can never fire for those paths -- a caught rejection is not an unhandled one. So instrumenting this suite has materially less effect than the others until the catch itself is reworked. That is a further argument for keeping both Tier-D suites LAST in the adoption order.
[2026-09-06 21:18] RESOLVED for both named suites, AND the detector found 36 MORE. terminal-async-output is now wired into deploy.sh gate 3.8 (12 members, was 11) and gen-catalog confirms it derives as GATE. md100-cmdlet-help demoted to '@catalog status TOOL' with a header note explaining it is NOT wired yet for a real reason: its top-level catch exits 2 on any harness error and seven post-verify call sites read rc 2 as 'puppeteer unavailable, SKIP' with no divergence flag, so wiring it as-is converts a harness error into a silent skip. Fix that catch to exit 1 with a 'harness fault' marker -- the marker deploy.sh gate 3.7 and post-verify 4f now branch on -- and THEN wire it. THE GENERALISED FIX IS THE REAL RESULT: gen-catalog.py now reports any script whose HAND-WRITTEN '@catalog status GATE' contradicts its DERIVED wiring column. That closes the exact loophole this task exposed -- the wiring column cannot lie because it is derived from the tree, but the status tag is hand-typed, and the status tag is what a reader trusts. Reported, deliberately NOT a hard failure, because the honest remedy is sometimes to wire it and sometimes to demote the header and the generator cannot know which. FIRST RUN OF THE NEW CHECK: **38 scripts DECLARE GATE while nothing invokes them** -- 25 ORPHAN (nothing references them at all), 8 CALLED (referenced by code but by no gate), 5 DOCS-ONLY. Against 1196 scripts of which only 42 are genuinely gate-wired, that means NEARLY HALF of everything claiming gate status is not a gate. The two in this task were the tip. Each of the 38 needs the same wire-or-demote call; they are now listed by every catalog regeneration instead of waiting to be stumbled over.
